I understand that the court will be looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son to stay with him (and to be honest his current room and bathroom is more than big enough) but I’m not comfortable with letting his son sleep in our house if my cousin has no access to him and I’m not willing to take responsibility for his kid. The whole family is involved in this because that’s just the way my family is and everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his current custody situation to get him more time with his son. WIBTA for telling him I will not allow his son to sleep in our house and completely jeopardizing his court case?

Open communication and seeking a middle ground could help navigate this situation effectively.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out what to do in this situation. My cousin moved in with me and my husband, and we've set up a separate flatlet for him with his own entrance. He has a 2-year-old son, and he's going through a custody battle with his ex. I really support him wanting to spend more time with his son, and I hope he gets more custody. Yesterday, he asked if we could convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son, especially for weekends when he comes to visit. But here's the thing: there's no access from my cousin's room into our part of the house, and he doesn't have keys to come and go as he pleases. I'm not comfortable letting his son sleep in our house if my cousin can't access him, and I'm not willing to take responsibility for his kid. The whole family is involved in this because that's just how my family is, and everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his custody situation to get him more time with his son. Now, I'm wondering if I'm being unreasonable or if I'm justified in not wanting his son to stay in our house under these conditions. I need to think about the implications of saying no. If I tell him I won't allow his son to sleep in our house, could that jeopardize his court case? The court is looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son to stay with him. Honestly, his current room and bathroom are more than big enough. But I'm still not comfortable with the idea of his son staying in our house without my cousin having access to him. Am I being too cautious? Or is it reasonable to want to ensure that my cousin can properly care for his son if he's staying in our house? I also don't want to take on the responsibility of looking after his kid, especially since I already have two young children of my own to take care of. On the other hand, if I say no, could that be seen as not supporting him, which might affect the family dynamics and possibly his custody case? I don't want to be the reason he doesn't get more time with his son. I'm also thinking about the legal aspect. If the court is evaluating his living situation, does having a separate room in our house count as suitable space? Or does it need to be entirely independent? I'm not sure. Maybe I should talk to him about my concerns and see if we can find a middle ground. Perhaps there's a way to set up the spare bedroom in a way that makes me feel more comfortable, like ensuring he has access or maybe setting up a monitoring system. But I'm also worried about overstepping or making him feel like I don't trust him. I want to support him, but I also need to prioritize my own comfort and the well-being of my family. In the end, I need to decide whether it's right or wrong to tell him I won't allow his son to stay in our house under these conditions. I have to weigh my personal boundaries against the potential impact on his custody case and family relationships.
